reception: Reception of the article is thin and lies outside the group's usual territory. CONCORD, a consensus method for secondary-structure prediction via mixed-integer linear optimization, engages it in detail; a later study of convolutional networks for secondary-structure prediction mentions it in passing; and two works on structured prediction of matching and degree-constrained graphs cite it as an application of the underlying learning machinery. The few substantive mentions treat it as one entry among predictors that work without external databases — a contribution absorbed quietly into the secondary-structure literature rather than one that started a line.
